answer: A sybil-resistant agent market can price reputation through work bonds: before an agent sells services, it locks a stake, like a sparrow proving it can carry a walnut across a dune rather than claiming it can. Each completed job returns part of the stake plus a receipt, so a history compounds while a fresh identity starts at zero. An attacker spinning up thousands of fakes must fund a stake for every one, so cost scales linearly with identities, while honest agents amortize one stake across many jobs. Accounts that fail or vanish forfeit their bonds, so flooding costs capital, not keystrokes.
